docs.title: UST Alumni Portal — Stakeholder Hub
docs.text:
Welcome to the planning and design documentation for the University of St. Thomas Alumni Digital Experience Portal — a personalized, widget-driven alumni portal built on Salesforce Experience Cloud.

This site is the living reference for stakeholders, product owners, and contributors. It covers what we're building, why, and what decisions still need to be made.

docs.title: What We're Building
docs.text:
The portal replaces the legacy alumni directory with a personalized, self-service experience that surfaces content relevant to each alumnus — their events, giving history, career connections, and campus updates — based on their unique profile in Salesforce.

Key principles:

  • Widget-driven — every section is a drag-and-drop component that site builders control in Experience Builder, no code changes needed for layout or navigation
  • Personalized — content adapts to the logged-in alumnus's college, giving history, event participation, location, and stated preferences
  • Salesforce-native — built on Experience Cloud LWR, using Lightning Web Components and the Higher Education Data Architecture (EDA)

docs.title: Usage Guidelines
docs.text:
• Dark Purple + Medium Purple should dominate any UST design
  • Bright Purple is an accent — use sparingly alongside the primaries
  • Emerald Green reflects the heritage of founder John Ireland; use as an accent with strong accessibility contrast
  • Cool Gray works for text, borders, and neutral backgrounds
  • Cool Gray @ 10% (#f3f3f3) is recommended as a default page background
  • Tints are intended for data visualization (charts, graphs) and background fills — not as replacements for the primary palette in UI chrome

docs.title: Connected Alumni Profile & Favorites — Implementation Plan
docs.text: Status: Approved, in progress. Recorded so context survives a session reset. Created: 2026-09-15

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Alumni Directory, Business (Professional) Directory, and Alumni News are currently three siloed browsing experiences. An alumnus's business listing, news mentions, and directory profile are functionally related (all keyed off the same Contact) but nothing on screen shows that relationship — you can't land on one alum and see everything connected to them. Additionally, there's no way for an alum to curate attention toward specific people or businesses they care about (no connection/favoriting feature exists at all).

docs.title: Requirements (confirmed via discussion)
docs.text:
• Alumni_Directory__c remains the protected, field-scoped gateway in front of Contact — no new code should read Contact fields directly for another user's profile; all cross-object joins happen in Apex, keyed off Contact Id but exposed only through Alumni_Directory__c- scoped DTOs, matching the existing AlumniProfileController pattern.
  • No visibility gating beyond "logged in." Any authenticated alum can view any other alum's connected profile — this is existing behavior (getProfileByRecordId has no opt-in check) and stays as-is.
  • Data model relationships between Alumni_Directory__c, Alumni_News__c, and Professional_Directory__c are not being restructured. Apex is the integration layer that bridges them via Contact Id. No schema re-pointing (e.g. Professional_Directory__c.Alumni__c stays pointed at Contact, not Alumni_Directory__c).
  • Two separate Experience Builder page experiences (deliberately not one branching route, so each can be curated independently):
  • My Profile (owned) — self-service editing (existing alumniProfile capability), plus "my favorites" list.
  • Alumni Connections / View Profile (others) — read-only discovery view: profile info, their business listings, their news mentions — each as independent, LMC-coordinated LWCs rather than one monolithic component.
  • New feature: Favorites — a one-directional, private curation list. An alum can favorite another alum's profile or a business listing.
  • No mutual visibility ("I would probably not show an alumni who has favorited them — that might seem creepy").
  • No notifications, no aggregate/social-proof counts in v1 ("keep it functional for the moment with an eye for iteration later").
  • Feeds a "your favorites" list on My Profile. A fast-follow goal (explicitly not v1 scope) is surfacing news/updates from favorited people/businesses on that list.
  • Favorite data model: one generic junction object (Alumni_Favorite__c), not multiple type-specific junctions ("I don't want to make a lot of objects for this junction and this could possibly help with other junctions for alumni in the future"). Shape:
  • Owner_Contact__c — Lookup(Contact), the person who favorited something.
  • Target_Type__c — Picklist (Alumni_Directory, Professional_Directory; extensible).
  • Target_Record_Id__c — Text(18).
  • Resolved entirely in Apex; no declarative lookup/relationship integrity to the target.
  • Correction found during build: Salesforce rejects a unique constraint on a formula field, so a formula-based Dedupe_Key__c (Owner+Type+TargetId) is not possible declaratively. Duplicate-favorite prevention is instead enforced in AlumniFavoriteController via an existence check before insert (see Task 2).
  • Favorite toggle UI: one small, reusable, embeddable LWC (ustFavoriteToggle) taking @api targetType and @api targetRecordId, dropped into alumniDirectoryList, alumniNewsList, and alumniBusinessDirectory.
  • Cross-widget coordination on the "View Profile" page uses a Lightning Message Channel, not URL state, not record Ids in the address bar ("I'd rather not have ids in the clear and don't think of these as shareable links"). Selecting an alum from a list publishes a message; the profile detail, business list, and news list widgets subscribe and refresh. Accepted tradeoff: no deep-linking/shareable URLs, no refresh-persistence of the selected profile.

docs.title: Research Notes
docs.text:
• Lightning Message Service is confirmed as the correct mechanism for same-page, cross- component pub/sub on LWR sites. It does not persist across navigation/refresh — this matches the "no URL state" decision, so there's no gap to design around.
  • AlumniProfileController.getProfileByRecordId() already resolves Contact → business directory records safely (WITH USER_MODE, without sharing with explicit ownership checks gating writes only). This is the pattern to extend for news, and to replicate for the new "view others" controller path.
  • Alumni_News__c carries both Contact__c and Alumni_Directory__c lookups (redundant). New query logic standardizes on Contact__c (matching Professional_Directory__c.Alumni__c) so one Contact Id resolves all three related objects consistently. The existing Alumni_Directory__c lookup on news stays untouched/unused by new logic — no data model changes.
  • Existing privacy/approval gates to preserve exactly as-is when re-querying for the unified view:
  • Alumni News: Reviewed_for_Community_Display__c = true AND Public_Display__c = true (see AlumniNewsListController.generateWhere).
  • Business Directory: RecordTypeId = Alumni_Business AND Company_Status__c = 'Approved' AND UST_Test_Contact__c = false (see AlumniBusinessDirectoryController.buildWhereClause).

docs.title: Task 1: Create the Alumni_Favorite__c object and deploy it — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Stand up the generic junction object so later tasks have a real target to write Apex against.
  • Implementation guidance: Fields — Owner_Contact__c (Lookup to Contact, required), Target_Type__c (Picklist: Alumni_Directory, Professional_Directory; restricted, extensible later), Target_Record_Id__c (Text(18), required). Sharing model: Private — personal curation data, visible only to the owner (and admins). Originally planned a formula-based Dedupe_Key__c field marked unique for declarative duplicate prevention; Salesforce deploy rejected this ("Can not specify unique for CustomFields that have a formula"). Removed that field — duplicate-favorite prevention is now an Apex-level existence check in AlumniFavoriteController (Task 2), not a schema constraint.
  • Test requirements: N/A (metadata only) — deployed to dev scratch org (UST-Alumni-Digital-Experience-Site__dev / CCI alias dev) via cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/objects/Alumni_Favorite__c --org dev.
  • Demo: Deploy succeeded ([Success]: Succeeded). Verified queryable via sf data query --query "SELECT Id FROM Alumni_Favorite__c LIMIT 1" against the dev org (0 rows, as expected for a fresh object). Not yet deployed to eda-staging — will push there after the full feature is validated end-to-end in the scratch org, per user direction.

docs.title: Task 2: Build AlumniFavoriteController Apex with add/remove/list methods, test-driven — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Apex service layer for favoriting — add, remove, "is this favorited by me," and "list my favorites."
  • Implementation guidance: without sharing (mirroring AlumniProfileController's rationale) since Alumni_Favorite__c is Private and community users need to manage only their own records — but explicitly filter every query/DML by the running user's resolved Contact Id, never trusting a passed-in owner Id from the client. Methods: isFavorited(String targetType, Id targetRecordId), addFavorite(...), removeFavorite(...), getMyFavorites() returning a DTO list resolved to display-friendly info (name/label) by branching on Target_Type__c. Wrote tests first (happy path, duplicate-add is idempotent/ no-op, removing a non-existent favorite is a no-op, cross-user isolation, orphaned-target handling, unsupported-type rejection).
  • Test requirements: AlumniFavoriteController_TEST.cls — 10 tests, all passing, 85% coverage on AlumniFavoriteController (org-wide bar is 75%; remaining gap is defensive early-return guards, not core logic).
  • Demo: sf apex run test --class-names AlumniFavoriteController_TEST --target-org UST-Alumni-Digital-Experience-Site__dev --result-format human --code-coverage --wait 20 → 10/10 pass, 85% coverage.

Real-world corrections hit while building this task (all resolved, recorded for context recovery): 1. TestAlumniCommunityDataFactory could not be reused. It requires a System Administrator user literally named ETL User and a profile named Alumni Community User — neither exists in this scratch org yet (confirmed live), matching the known gotcha in AGENTS.md. The new test class builds its own lightweight, self-contained data instead of depending on that factory or org-provisioning state. 2. A plain internal/Standard User cannot have ContactId set — FIELD_INTEGRITY_EXCEPTION, only portal users can be associated to a contact. Only users on a portal-licensed profile can be linked to a Contact. Test users now use the Customer Community Login User profile (a standard, always-available portal profile) with an Account on each test Contact (portal users require one). 3. A fresh custom object grants zero access to non-admin profiles by default. A new Alumni_Favorites_User permission set was added, granting object CRUD on Alumni_Favorite__c and Read on the small field set getMyFavorites() resolves from Alumni_Directory__c/Professional_Directory__c (Name/First_Name_Text__c/ Last_Name_Text__c/Class_Year_Text__c and Company_Name__c/Company_City__c/ Company_State__c respectively). This is deployed alongside the Apex classes. - All three Alumni_Favorite__c fields are required, so no field-level permission entries are possible on it — Salesforce rejects granting field permissions on required fields (deploy error: "You cannot deploy to a required field"). Object-level CRUD alone is sufficient since required fields are implicitly editable whenever Create/Edit is granted at the object level. 4. Dead end, recorded so it isn't re-investigated: the only profile in this scratch org with "Alumni" in its name (Alumni Profile) turned out to be a Guest User License profile, not a logged-in community profile — it cannot be assigned to a real User at all. Also confirmed live: none of the standard Customer Community* profiles have any pre-existing FieldPermissions/ObjectPermissions grant on Alumni_Directory__c or Professional_Directory__c in this org. Whatever grants let AlumniProfileController/ AlumniBusinessDirectoryController work for real alumni today must live on a site-specific profile this scratch org hasn't been provisioned with yet (likely set up directly in Setup UI, not tracked in this repo's source) — not something to chase further for test purposes; the new permission set sidesteps it entirely. 5. PermissionSetAssignment DML in @TestSetup must be isolated in its own System.runAs block — inserting it in the same transaction as regular sObject DML (Account/Contact/Alumni_Directory__c/etc.) throws MIXED_DML_OPERATION (setup vs. non-setup object). Wrapped in System.runAs(new User(Id = UserInfo.getUserId())) to isolate it, which is the standard pattern for this restriction inside test methods.

Deployed to dev scratch org only (Alumni_Favorite__c, AlumniFavoriteController, AlumniFavoriteController_TEST, Alumni_Favorites_User permission set). Not yet pushed to eda-staging.

docs.title: Task 3: Build reusable ustFavoriteToggle LWC — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: One small, embeddable favorite/unfavorite button component.
  • Implementation guidance: @api targetType, @api targetRecordId. On connect, calls isFavorited (imperative, not @wire, since the initial load also needs error handling and a loading flag) to set initial icon state (utility:add outline vs. utility:favorite filled, via lightning-button-icon). Click calls addFavorite/removeFavorite imperatively, optimistic UI update with rollback to the prior state on error. Emits a favoritechange custom event ({ targetType, targetRecordId, isFavorited }) for optional parent reaction (not consumed yet, but free to add now for Task 4/8).
  • Test requirements: ustFavoriteToggle.test.js — 8 tests: unfavorited render, favorited render, add-on-click, remove-on-click, event dispatch, rollback+error on add failure, rollback+error on remove failure, error+safe-default on initial load failure, disabled/no-op when required props are missing. All passing (npm test -- --testPathPattern=ustFavoriteToggle → 4 suites incl. this one, 24/24 tests pass, no regressions in the 3 existing suites it shares a test run with).
  • Demo: Deployed to dev scratch org (cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc/ustFavoriteToggle --org dev → [Success]: Succeeded). Functional verification done via the Jest suite against the real compiled component (mocking only the three Apex methods) rather than a manual Experience-Builder placement, since Jest already exercises every state transition end-to-end; a standalone page placement is deferred to Task 4, where the component gets embedded into real list rows and can be checked in context.

docs.title: Task 4: Embed ustFavoriteToggle into alumniDirectoryList, alumniNewsList, and alumniBusinessDirectory — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Make favoriting available everywhere per requirement — "favoriting could happen a lot of places."
  • Implementation guidance: Each list item row gets one <c-ust-favorite-toggle> with the right target-type/target-record-id (Alumni_Directory Id for directory/news rows, Professional_Directory Id for business rows). Purely additive markup + minor CSS — no changes to existing Apex controllers for these lists.
  • alumniDirectoryList: new "Favorite" column in the table, target-type="Alumni_Directory" keyed on al.key (already the Alumni_Directory__c Id).
  • alumniNewsList: toggle placed in the card header, target-type="Alumni_Directory" keyed on news.adId. Guarded with lwc:if={news.adId} — some news rows have no linked Alumni_Directory__c record, and the toggle is simply omitted for those rather than rendered disabled.
  • alumniBusinessDirectory: toggle placed at the top of each card, target-type= "Professional_Directory" keyed on record.Id. Since the whole card has onclick={openRecordModal} to open the detail modal, the toggle's wrapper div stops click propagation (stopFavoriteToggleClickPropagation, same pattern already used elsewhere in this component for the modal's inner-click guard) so favoriting a card doesn't also pop open its modal.
  • Test requirements: Extended alumniDirectoryList.test.js and alumniNewsList.test.js (previously only tested the exported resolveProfileNavigation pure function, with no component-render tests at all) with new describe blocks that mock the Apex list call, render the component with sample data, and assert c-ust-favorite-toggle elements exist with the correct targetType/targetRecordId per row - including a case in the news list where a row has no adId and correctly renders no toggle. alumniBusinessDirectory had no existing test file at all; added a new minimal one (alumniBusinessDirectory.test.js) scoped specifically to the toggle wiring and the click-propagation guard, not a full component rewrite (out of scope for this task). All passing: npm test → 5 suites, 29/29 tests, no regressions.
  • Demo: Deployed to dev scratch org (cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc --org dev → [Success]: Succeeded). Verified via the full Jest suite against the real compiled components rather than a manual browser walkthrough, since every row/card-level rendering path and the click-guard are already covered end-to-end.

docs.title: Task 5: Build getMyFavorites() display DTO + ustMyFavorites LWC on My Profile — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Let an alum see their curated list on their own profile page.
  • Implementation guidance: DTO resolves each favorite's Target_Type__c to a human label, name/title, and short subtitle (class year for alumni, city/industry for businesses). Group by type in the UI ("Alumni I'm Following," "Businesses I'm Following"). Deep-linking a favorited alum into the Connections page is optional polish, not blocking (would need to route through LMC since there's no URL/Id state by design) — deferred, not built in this task.
  • The DTO-building logic itself (toDtos()) already existed from Task 2's AlumniFavoriteController.getMyFavorites() — this task's remaining work was the LWC: ustMyFavorites calls getMyFavorites() on connect, splits the flat DTO list into alumniFavorites/businessFavorites by targetType, and renders each as its own section, only when that section has at least one entry (no empty "Businesses I'm Following" heading with nothing under it).
  • Orphaned favorites (target record deleted/archived) render a de-emphasized placeholder ("This alumni profile is no longer available" / "This business listing is no longer available") instead of blank text or silently disappearing, so the alumnus's favorite count always matches what's visibly listed.
  • Test requirements: Apex-side DTO-building coverage already existed from Task 2 (getMyFavorites_resolvesDisplayFields_forBothTargetTypes, getMyFavorites_marksOrphanedFavorite_whenTargetDeleted). New ustMyFavorites.test.js — 5 tests: empty state, grouped-by-type rendering with both sections, single-section rendering when only one type has favorites, orphaned-favorite placeholder, and error-message display on Apex failure. All passing (npm test → 6 suites, 34/34 tests, no regressions).
  • Demo: Deployed to dev scratch org (cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc/ustMyFavorites --org dev → [Success]: Succeeded, after fixing a first-attempt deploy failure — see correction below). Verified via the Jest suite against the real compiled component; not yet placed on an actual Experience Builder page (that happens in Task 9, once both My Profile and Alumni Connections pages are assembled together).

Real-world correction hit while building this task: the LWC bundle's <description> in *.js-meta.xml has a hard 255-character limit (LightningComponentBundle metadata field) — the first deploy attempt failed with Value too long for field: Description maximum length is:255. Shortened the description to fit; no functional impact.

docs.title: Task 6: Build AlumniConnectionsController Apex — read-only connected profile query, test-driven — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Server-side logic for the View Profile page: given a target Contact Id, return Alumni_Directory__c-scoped profile fields, news mentions, and business listings in one call.
  • Implementation guidance: New class (separate from AlumniProfileController, which is scoped to "my own" + canEdit semantics). Reuses existing field-scoping discipline — same limited Alumni_Directory__c field set already exposed today. Queries Alumni_News__c by Contact__c with the same Reviewed_for_Community_Display__c/Public_Display__c gate. Queries Professional_Directory__c by Alumni__c with the full gate confirmed by re-reading AlumniBusinessDirectoryController.buildWhereClause directly (not from memory) - RecordTypeId = Alumni_Business, Alumni__c != null, Company_Status__c = 'Approved', and UST_Test_Contact__c = false (the plan draft had only listed Company_Status__c; re-checking the source before writing code caught the missing RecordTypeId/ UST_Test_Contact__c conditions before they became a real gap). Wrote tests first: all- three-present, none-present, news-only, unpublished news excluded (both failure combinations - reviewed-but-not-public, and public-but-not-reviewed), unapproved business excluded, test-contact-flagged business excluded, no-directory-record and null-Contact-Id edge cases.
  • Test requirements: AlumniConnectionsController_TEST.cls — 9 tests, all passing, 93% coverage on AlumniConnectionsController (target was ≥90%). Explicit assertions that every existing privacy/approval gate is respected.
  • Demo: sf apex run test --class-names AlumniConnectionsController_TEST --target-org UST-Alumni-Digital-Experience-Site__dev --result-format human --code-coverage --wait 20 → 9/9 pass, 93% coverage.

Real-world corrections hit while building this task: 1. Professional_Directory__c.UST_Test_Contact__c is a formula field rolling up Alumni__r.UST_Test_Contact__c (a Contact field that exists live in this org but is not tracked in this repo's Contact metadata source) — it cannot be set directly on insert (Field is not writeable). Test data instead sets UST_Test_Contact__c = true on the linked Contact, letting the formula roll up naturally, exactly mirroring how a real test contact would be flagged. 2. Professional_Directory__c.Company_Status__c restricted picklist does not include a 'Pending' value in this org — active values, queried live rather than assumed (getPicklistValues()), are Submitted, Under Review, Approved, Inactive. Test data uses 'Submitted' for the not-yet-approved case.

docs.title: Task 7: Build the AlumniSelection Lightning Message Channel + ustAlumniConnectionProfile detail LWC — ✅ Done
docs.text:
• Objective: Cross-widget sync mechanism, plus the read-only detail view widget.
  • Implementation guidance: Defined AlumniSelection.messageChannel-meta.xml with payload { contactId } (in-memory only — never written to a URL). ustAlumniConnectionProfile subscribes via @wire(MessageContext) + subscribe, shows a distinct empty/prompt state until a message arrives (showPromptState), a separate empty state if the selected contact has no public profile (showEmptyState), then calls AlumniConnectionsController and renders profile fields, news mentions, and business listings, plus an embedded favorite toggle for the viewed alum (Alumni_Directory toggle in the header, one Professional_Directory toggle per business listing).
  • Test requirements: ustAlumniConnectionProfile.test.js — 5 tests: prompt state before any selection, full render after a selection message (profile fields, news, business listings, and both favorite toggles with correct targetType/targetRecordId), empty state when no profile is found, error message on Apex failure, and re-query when a second selection message arrives for a different contact. All passing (npm test → 7 suites, 39/39 tests, no regressions).
  • Demo: Deployed to dev scratch org — message channel first (cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/messageChannels --org dev), then the LWC that depends on it (cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc/ustAlumniConnectionProfile --org dev), both [Success]: Succeeded after fixing a first-attempt failure (see correction below). Verified via the Jest suite, which directly captures the subscribe() listener callback and invokes it to simulate a publish from another widget — a real end-to-end two-widget page wiring happens in Task 8/9.

Real-world corrections hit while building this task: 1. LightningMessageChannel.description has the same 255-character limit already hit on LightningComponentBundle in Task 5 — first deploy attempt failed with the same Value too long for field: Description maximum length is:255 error. Shortened it. 2. Deploying the LWC before the message channel deploy succeeded failed with a confusing downstream error (Unable to retrieve metadata for descriptor: markup://c:__LightningMessageChannel__AlumniSelection__c) — the component imports @salesforce/messageChannel/AlumniSelection__c, which requires the channel to already exist server-side. Deploy order matters here: message channel first, then any LWC that references it. 3. lightning-formatted-rich-text's stubbed Jest behavior — like the lightning-button label gotcha already documented in AGENTS.md, this base component's value prop is not reflected into textContent in the Jest stub environment. Asserted on .value directly instead of searching rendered text for the news body.

docs.title: Task 8: Wire list components as LMC publishers on the View Profile page
docs.text:
• Objective: Clicking an alum anywhere on the page updates the shared detail widget instead of navigating away.
  • Implementation guidance: Add a new @api flag (mirroring the existing useNewProfileLink pattern already in alumniDirectoryList/alumniNewsList) — e.g. useMessageChannel — so clicking a row publishes to the LMC instead of navigating via NavigationMixin. Keeps existing navigate-to-record-page behavior intact for any other placement of these components (backward compatible).
  • Test requirements: Extend existing Jest tests to cover the new publish-on-click branch without breaking existing navigation-branch tests.
  • Demo: On the View Profile page, clicking an alum in directory/business/news lists updates the shared detail widget in place, no page reload.

docs.title: Task 9: Assemble the two Experience Builder pages and do an end-to-end walkthrough
docs.text:
• Objective: Ship the actual page experiences.
  • Implementation guidance: My Profile page — existing alumniProfile (owned mode) + new ustMyFavorites. Alumni Connections page — alumniDirectoryList/alumniNewsList/ alumniBusinessDirectory (search/browse side) + ustAlumniConnectionProfile (detail side), all wired to the shared LMC, favorite toggles throughout. Confirm placement approach (direct Experience Builder placement vs. forcing through the UST_Portal_Widget__c zone registry) fits naturally before committing to one — these are more bespoke than the generic zone pattern and may not need to go through it.
  • Test requirements: Manual QA — favorite an alum from the directory list, confirm it shows on My Profile; click through directory → business → news on the Connections page and confirm the detail widget follows each selection; confirm a logged-in alum cannot see another's edit controls.
  • Demo: Full user journey — log in, browse Alumni Connections, click into a few different alumni (seeing their business + news alongside their profile), favorite a couple, navigate to My Profile, see the favorites list populated.

docs.text:

  • A personalized activity feed of news/updates from favorited people/businesses on My Profile (fast-follow candidate, not blocking this plan).

docs.title: UST Alumni Digital Experience Site — Main Guide
Purpose
docs.text: Rebuild the University of St. Thomas alumni portal on Salesforce Experience Cloud, replacing the legacy alumni directory with a personalized, widget-driven experience. Logged-in alumni see content tailored to their profile data — giving history, event registrations, major/college, geographic location, and self-declared preferences.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text:
• Salesforce Experience Cloud — LWR (Lightning Web Runtime) site, NOT Aura (LWR Sites for Experience Cloud docs)
  • LWR provides better performance, modern routing, and first-class LWC support compared to Aura-based sites
  • Uses the enhanced_lwr template in sfdx-project.json; do not use aura or aloha templates
  • LWC widgets as the primary UI building block (LWR sites require LWC — Aura components are not supported)
  • EDA (Higher Education Data Architecture) managed package provides the academic data model (affiliations, programs, etc.)
  • SSO: Federated ID on Community User record maps to alumni personal email

docs.title: Widget-First Design
docs.text:
Every section of the portal is a self-contained LWC "widget" component. The portal uses a record-driven widget zone system to control which widgets appear, on which pages, in what order, and for which audience segments — admins manage this through UST_Portal_Widget__c records, without touching Experience Builder or code.

See WIDGET-CATALOG.md for the full widget inventory and component registry. See Widget Zone System below for implementation and configuration details.

docs.title: Widget Zone System
docs.text:
Replaces the legacy EASY Widgets pattern with an admin-facing Salesforce object. Admins create and edit UST_Portal_Widget__c records to control the portal without any deployment.

Flow:

Admin creates/edits UST_Portal_Widget__c record
  Zone = body | Page = home | Component = ust_profile_card | Sort = 10 | Audience = All
         |
Experience Builder page loads ustWidgetZone (zoneName="body", pageContext="home")
         |
PortalWidgetController.getWidgetsForZone() queries active matching records
  - filters by zone, page context, and current user's audience segments
  - returns ordered list of widget DTOs
         |
ustWidgetZone renders each widget in sort order
  - registered component  →  renders the real widget LWC
  - unregistered component →  renders ustPortalWidgetStub
       (stub is visible in Experience Builder, invisible in the live site)

Files involved:

File Role objects/UST_Portal_Widget__c/ Object + 7 field definitions classes/PortalWidgetController.cls Apex — queries widgets, checks audience segments lwc/ustWidgetZone/ Host container — drag onto pages in Experience Builder lwc/ustPortalWidgetStub/ Dev placeholder — Builder-visible, live-site-invisible

docs.title: Experience Builder Setup
docs.text:
Place one UST Widget Zone component per zone on each page:

  1. Open Experience Builder → from the component panel, drag UST Widget Zone onto the page
  2. In the component property panel, set:
  3. Zone Name — one of: body, sidebar, banner, above_footer
  4. Page Context — the page slug, e.g. home, events, giving, profile
  5. Repeat for each zone on that page
  6. Publish the site after placing zones

The same UST Widget Zone component is placed on every page. Different Zone Name + Page Context values on each instance mean each zone only loads the records targeting it.

docs.title: Configuring Widget Records
docs.text:
Create UST_Portal_Widget__c records via Setup → Object Manager → UST Portal Widget → Records, or create a List View for easy admin access.

Field Purpose Example Widget Name Admin label — be descriptive Profile Card - Home Page Zone Which zone instance renders this widget body Page Context Pages where this widget appears (multi-select) home; profile Component Name Registry key — selects the LWC to render ust_profile_card Sort Order Position within the zone; lower numbers appear first 10, 20, 30 Audience Rule Which alumni segment sees this widget All Is Active Kill switch — uncheck to hide without deleting ✓ Description Admin notes; not shown to alumni (optional)

A widget that should appear on multiple pages uses one record — select multiple values in Page Context rather than duplicating the record.

docs.title: Audience Rules
docs.text:
Rule Current State Notes All ✅ Active Shown to every authenticated user Donor ⏳ Stubbed Awaiting Contact donor flag field confirmation (see DATA-MODEL.md) Parent ⏳ Stubbed Awaiting Contact parent flag field confirmation Faculty_Staff ⏳ Stubbed Awaiting Contact faculty/staff flag confirmation

To activate a stubbed rule: confirm the Contact field API name with the advancement team, then un-comment the corresponding block in PortalWidgetController.resolveUserAudiences().

A user who qualifies for multiple segments sees widgets for all of them. Create separate records for widgets that target one segment but not all alumni (e.g. a Donor-only tile alongside an All-alumni tile in the same zone).

docs.title: Adding a New Widget to the Registry
docs.text:
When a new widget LWC is built and deployed, activate it in the zone system with three changes:

1 — Add the boolean flag to WIDGET_REGISTRY in ustWidgetZone.js: 

// In the WIDGET_REGISTRY constant at the top of the file:
const WIDGET_REGISTRY = {
    ust_static_content: 'isStaticContent',   // ← already active
    ust_profile_card:   'isProfileCard',     // ← uncomment when built
};

2 — Add a lwc:if (or lwc:elseif) block in ustWidgetZone.html, above the lwc:else stub: 

<!-- First registered widget: use lwc:if -->
<template lwc:if={widget.isStaticContent}>
    <c-ust-static-content rich-text-content={widget.staticContent}></c-ust-static-content>
</template>
<!-- Additional widgets: use lwc:elseif -->
<template lwc:elseif={widget.isProfileCard}>
    <c-ust-profile-card></c-ust-profile-card>
</template>
<!-- Keep this stub block as the final lwc:else — catches any unregistered component names -->
<template lwc:else>
    <c-ust-portal-widget-stub ...></c-ust-portal-widget-stub>
</template>

3 — Deploy both the zone and the new widget together: 

cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc/ustWidgetZone --org dev
cci task run deploy --path force-app/main/default/lwc/ustProfileCard --org dev

No Experience Builder changes are needed. The zone component already on the page calls the same Apex query and automatically renders the real widget the next time the page loads.

Stub behavior: Until Step 1–2 are deployed, a widget record with Widget_Type__c = ust_profile_card renders the stub placeholder (visible in Builder, invisible to alumni in the live site). This lets admins configure records ahead of the LWC being built.

Dynamic imports are NOT supported in this org's API version. The static lwc:if/lwc:elseif chain in ustWidgetZone.html is the correct pattern. Do not use import() or lwc:is — they will fail with LWC1503.

docs.title: Portal Widget Authoring Experience — Implementation Plan
docs.text: Status: Phases A and 0 done (deployed to the dev scratch org, not yet committed to git). Phases 1–3 approved, not started. Recorded so context survives a session reset. Created: 2026-10-14. Dev org: UST-Alumni-Digital-Experience-Site__dev (CCI alias dev), expires 2026-10-27.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Give portal admins a purpose-built authoring layout for UST_Portal_Widget__c (replacing the classic page layout) with a rich text editor that behaves like the Experience Builder one, plus the things clients actually need in widget content: call-to-action buttons, personalization data tags, and later a hero image widget backed by the S3 upload tool.

Guiding decision: structured data beats markup in the rich text. Buttons are JSON on the record and rendered by our component (not HTML/classes inside Quill). That removed the need for a custom Quill build and for a per-paragraph class list.

docs.title: Phase A — DONE: Editor layout, headings, widget style class
docs.text:
Built, browser-verified in the dev org, 67 Jest tests passing, Apex tests passing.

Piece File(s) Record-page layout (Widget Setup / Content / Audience Filters, live preview) lwc/ustWidgetRecordEditor/ Rich text editor with Paragraph + Heading 2–5 dropdown, char counter, H1/H6 warning lwc/ustRichTextEditor/ Renders content; applies allowlisted widget style class lwc/ustStaticContent/ Widget style picklist (Callout Panel, Purple Banner, Centered, Muted) fields/Content_CSS_Class__c Record page, set as the View override flexipages/UST_Portal_Widget_Record_Page, UST_Portal_Widget__c.object-meta.xml Admin permission set (new fields are invisible without FLS) permissionsets/UST_Portal_Widget_Admin DTO carries contentCssClass PortalWidgetController, ustWidgetZone Apex tests force-app/tests/default/classes/PortalWidgetController_TEST.cls

Also done in the same session: API version bumped to 68.0 everywhere (sfdx-project.json, cumulusci.yml, all *-meta.xml); WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED (removed in API 68) replaced with WITH USER_MODE in four controllers; Code Analyzer High findings fixed.

docs.title: Gotchas learned (do not re-discover)
docs.text:
• lightning-input-rich-text limits. Allowed formats include header/link/image/code/blockquote/ script/direction/table, but toolbar buttons exist only for bold/italic/underline/strike, lists, indent, left/center/right align, link, image, clear. setFormat() only accepts align, background, bold, code, code-block, color, font, header (1–6), italic, link, size, strike, underline. No access to the Quill instance, modules, registries, or selection events. class attributes cannot round-trip.
  • getFormat() steals focus. It refocuses the editor, closing the heading dropdown and the Link dialog. Cursor-sync handlers are on a wrapper around only the rich text, and toolbar clicks (clientY < TOOLBAR_HEIGHT_PX) pause tracking for 8 s (TOOLBAR_PAUSE_MS). composedPath() does not expose .ql-editor, so geometry is the only way to tell toolbar from text.
  • Combobox change bubbles out of the child component and was mistaken for a content change ("h3" replaced the body). Both handlers call event.stopPropagation().
  • The editor textbox only exists after a real mouse click in the editor area (lazy init) — matters for Playwright tests.
  • Stale Lightning bundles after a JS-only deploy. Clear localStorage/sessionStorage, IndexedDB and Cache Storage, reload, wait ~20 s, reload again (repeat once if needed).
  • cci task run deploy can say "Succeeded" and deploy nothing (new field was missing). Use sf project deploy start --source-dir ... and verify with a query.
  • New fields need FLS. Admin sees nothing until UST_Portal_Widget_Admin is assigned.
  • Apex tests in the scratch org: ~80 pre-existing failures are environmental (Network is UnderConstruction; Alumni Community User profile and ETL User missing → "List index out of bounds"; Alumni_Business record type unavailable to admin). Not caused by code changes. Finish the config_dev flow to make them meaningful.
  • Jest + base component stubs: field-name/label are properties, not attributes — query all elements and filter on the property.

docs.title: Decisions (confirmed 2026-10-14)
docs.text: Topic Decision Editor Stay on the base lightning-input-rich-text. Full Quill (static resource) only if per-paragraph classes or inline images become a real requirement. Buttons JSON on the widget record, rendered by our component. Placement Above or Below the text (default Below). No limit on count. Button types External URL and Portal link (site menu item or typed relative path). Relative paths required so content migrates sandbox → prod. Button sizing Handled by the widget content CSS class, so buttons stay consistent. No per-button size field. Data tags {{Tag}} syntax, sourced from Alumni_Directory__c only, usable in header, body, button labels and button URLs. Tag fallback {{First_Name\|Alum}} — text after \| is used when the value is blank (and for guests). Sensitive tags Excluded (email, phone, birthdate, address) except Banner ID, which is allowed — including in URLs. Page-name mismatch We fix it (Phase 0).

docs.title: Phase 0 — Page context: fix the mismatch and keep it current (design agreed 2026-10-15)
docs.text:
Problem. ustWidgetZone derives the page context from CurrentPageReference (attributes.name, lowercased). Page_Context__c values are all, home, giving, events, profile, directory, news. Actual LWR page API names (from sfdc_cms__route): Home, alumni_directory__c, Alumni_Event_Creation__c, alumni_notes__c, business_directory__c, lawyer_search__c, my_account__c, My_Business__c, News_Detail__c, plus system pages (Login, Register, Error…). Only home matches; targeting a widget at "Directory" likely never matches.

Platform facts (verified in dev org). Site pages cannot be listed at runtime: DigitalExperience is not queryable, no Tooling object exposes routes, NetworkPageOverride covers standard pages only. Only NavigationMenuItem is queryable (menu pages only). So the list must be built by the site itself.

Where zones live today (from the repo bundle). body and sidebar are in individual page views (Home: body + sidebar; Alumni_Directory: sidebar). banner and above_footer are in the theme layout scopedHeaderAndFooter, i.e. on every page using that layout.

docs.title: Design: self-registering zone placements
docs.text:
1. New object UST_Portal_Zone_Placement__c: Page_Name__c (lowercased page API name, or * for "all pages"), Zone__c, Scope__c (Page / Layout), Page_Label__c (admin-editable friendly label), Last_Seen__c, Hidden__c; unique external-id key Page|Zone.
  2. Layout-level zones (decided 2026-10-15): no bundle change. banner and above_footer live in the scopedHeaderAndFooter theme layout (layout type Inner, used by 14 views; only the two error pages use snaThemeLayout). That layout also holds the built-in LWR navigation components and ustAlumniTheme, so content placed there already appears on every page — keep using those zones for "every page" content. A zone cannot detect by itself whether it is in a shared layout, so the registry has an admin-editable Scope__c (Page / Layout). Seed banner and above_footer as Layout (Page_Name__c = *) from this verified fact; admins can flip the flag for any future layout zone. (Optional later: a zoneScope builder property on ustWidgetZone so the builder sets it automatically — would require editing/redeploying the theme layout file; not needed now.)
  3. Registration happens only in Experience Builder (state.app === 'commeditor', already detected in ustWidgetZone). The zone calls a non-cacheable Apex method that upserts the placement. Live visitors and guests never write; Apex also refuses unless the user can create the object. Zero overhead for the public site. A zone whose existing placement is Layout-scoped keeps * and is not duplicated per page when an admin visits different pages.
  4. Editor behavior (ustWidgetRecordEditor):
  5. Zone is chosen first; the page picker lists only pages that have that zone, plus All pages.
  6. Changing the zone auto-removes known pages that lack the new zone, with a notice and Undo ("Removed Directory — no Sidebar zone on that page").
  7. Pages not yet registered are kept with a warning (lets admins pre-configure before a page exists).
  8. "Appears on: Home, Alumni Directory" coverage line; warning when a widget would appear nowhere.
  9. Free-text escape hatch for unregistered page names.
  10. Page_Context__c becomes an unrestricted multi-select picklist so INCLUDES keeps working while the custom editor can save any page name. (Verify in the spike that the API/LWC accepts values not in the list.)
  11. Seed the registry once from the 16 routes/views in the current bundle (script or CCI task), and add a one-time data migration for existing widget records: directory → alumni_directory__c, etc. giving, events, profile, news are left as-is for now (no matching route in the dev bundle; owner to check whether those pages exist in EDA-Staging before mapping or retiring them).
  12. The same registry feeds the Portal link picker for buttons (Phase 3).

docs.title: Limits to remember
docs.text:
• A zone removed in the builder is not detected (nothing runs). Show Last_Seen__c, flag stale entries, allow Hidden__c; do not delete automatically.
  • The registry reflects the builder state, which can be ahead of the published site.
  • Editor checks are advisory; records changed by data loader are not validated, and a mismatch simply means the widget does not render.
  • Unverified until built: that Apex DML works from the builder session, and unrestricted multi-select behavior.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm the mismatch in the dev org (widget on a non-home page → expect no render).
  2. Build the object, permission sets (admin: create/edit; no guest access), registration Apex, seed of the layout zones, and tests (Apex: guest/non-admin cannot register, upsert idempotent, * handling; Jest: builder-only registration).
  3. Editor page/zone picker, auto-remove with Undo, coverage line.
  4. Picklist change, migration, seed, docs (WIDGET-CATALOG.md, MAIN_GUIDE.md, PortalWidgetController_TEST).

docs.text:
1. Insert at cursor. Does lightning-input-rich-text.insertTextAtCursor() (documented as "reserved for internal use") reliably insert plain text {{First_Name}} at the cursor in the dev org? If not, fallback = append at end, or copy-to-clipboard.

NavigationMenuItem is queryable (7 InternalLink items in dev: /my-account, /alumni-directory, /alumni-notes, /lawyer-search, /business-directory, /my-business, /alumni-event-creation). Confirm the menu-item query works for the navigation set bound to the site (note sync_navigation_menu handles per-org set names).

docs.title: Tag registry (single source of truth, Apex)
docs.text:
Tag Source Allowed in URLs First_Name Nickname__c, else First_Name_Text__c no Last_Name Last_Name_Text__c no Class_Year Class_Year_Text__c no Employer Employer_Text__c no Job_Title Occupation_Text__c no St_Thomas_Degree St_Thomas_Degree_text__c no City_State City_State__c no Contact_Id Contact_ID__c (formula) yes Banner_ID Contact_Banner_ID__c (formula) yes

Excluded on purpose: email, phone, mobile, birthdate, mailing street/postal code/country, middle name. Registry is exposed via an @AuraEnabled method (label, token, sample value) so the editor dropdown and the Apex resolver cannot drift.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Syntax {{ Name }} or {{ Name|fallback }}. Case-insensitive; spaces ≡ underscores (matches the existing EASY/VF behavior in ApplicationUtilities.replaceDataTags).
  • Strict pattern that tolerates editor formatting inside a tag ({{First_<b>Name</b>}}): match \{\{((?:[^{}<]|<[^>]*>)+?)\}\}, strip tags from the capture, then parse name/fallback.
  • Blank value → fallback if given, else empty string. Guests and users with no directory record get blanks/fallbacks. Unknown tags are left literally in the text (and flagged to admins in the editor).
  • HTML-escape every substituted value. (The VF implementation inserts values unescaped; alumni can edit these fields themselves.) Header and button labels are plain text. Fallback text is escaped too.
  • In URLs: only tags marked "allowed in URLs" resolve, values are URL-encoded; other tags in a URL resolve to empty.
  • Resolve server-side in PortalWidgetController for the current user's Alumni_Directory__c (Contact__c = running user's ContactId), using a separate system-mode query of only the whitelisted fields. Do not add fields to the existing WITH USER_MODE directory query — a missing FLS on any new field would break the whole widget zone for portal users.
  • Applies to: Static_Content_Header__c, Static_Content__c, button labels and button URLs (and hero text later).

docs.text:
• "Insert data tag" dropdown beside Paragraph style (rich text) and beside the header input (plain input → setRangeText, which is straightforward).
  • Live warnings for unknown tag names.
  • Preview resolves tags with sample values from the registry.
  • Stretch: "Preview as" a chosen Alumni Directory record.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Apex: parsing (formatted/split tags, case, spaces), fallback, blank, guest, escaping (<script> in a value), URL encoding, URL-disallowed tags, unknown tags. Jest: insert dropdown, unknown-tag warning.

docs.text:
{
  "version": 1,
  "buttons": [
    {
      "id": "b1",
      "label": "Give today, {{First_Name|friend}}",
      "type": "external",
      "url": "https://example.edu/give?id={{Contact_Id}}",

Styles carried over from EASY Widget Button: text_link, brand, outline-brand, destructive, text-destructive, neutral, success. Alignment: left, center, end. Icon is optional and validated. No per-button size — sizing comes from the widget content CSS class.

docs.title: Link rules (enforced at save AND at render; Apex re-validates)
docs.text:
• External: https: only (plus mailto: / tel:). Reject javascript:, data:, etc. New tab → rel="noopener noreferrer".
  • Portal: must start with a single / (reject //); site base path is added at render time, so the same JSON works in sandbox and prod. Picker suggestions come from the site navigation menu; free typing of any relative path is allowed (covers /news/<id>).
  • Render real <a> elements (not <button>), visible focus, decorative icons, unique labels.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• ustWidgetButtonEditor (child of ustWidgetRecordEditor): add / edit / reorder / delete, saves with the record's Save (EASY writes immediately and cannot edit). Uses stable ids, not array index. Section shown for widget types that support buttons (extend COMPONENT_SECTIONS).
  • ustWidgetButtons (shared renderer): used by ustStaticContent now and the hero widget later.
  • Apex: parse/validate/sanitize JSON, drop invalid entries, resolve tags in label/url, return a clean list on PortalWidgetDto.
  • Widget content CSS classes get button-size rules so buttons stay consistent. Open item: Content_CSS_Class__c is single-select; if a widget needs e.g. "Callout panel" and "wide buttons", add a second picklist (e.g. Button_Size_Class__c) rather than multi-selecting.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Apex: JSON sanitization, scheme allowlist, relative path rules, tag resolution in labels/URLs. Jest: editor add/edit/reorder/delete, renderer placement above/below, unsafe URL rejection.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Later: hero image widget + S3
docs.text:
Not started; design notes only.

  • New widget type ust_hero_banner (add to Component_Name__c picklist, WIDGET_REGISTRY, and a lwc:elseif block in ustWidgetZone.html — see AGENTS.md "adding a widget").
  • Fields: image URL, alt text (required), overlay text (reuse ustRichTextEditor), buttons (reuse ustWidgetButtons), overlay scrim for contrast.
  • Image upload: embed the existing awsS3DirectoryImage LWC (dependency repo UniversityOfSaintThomas/Salesforce-LWC-S3-Integration, already in cumulusci.yml) in a new "Hero" section of ustWidgetRecordEditor, using the widget's own record Id and image field; fileNameSuffix allows desktop/mobile variants.
  • Suggested changes to the S3 tool: canvas output is always PNG (toDataURL() with no type) → use JPEG ~0.85 for photos; stored URL has no cache-buster so replaced images can look stale; consider CloudFront and a second smaller size. Base64-through-Apex is fine at hero sizes but not large files.
  • Setup needed per org: real bucket URL on the Named Credential and the CSP Trusted Site (img-src), AWS keys on the External Credential principal, republish the site, and assign AWS_S3_Directory_Image to widget admins.
  • Open questions: full-width vs fixed banner height / aspect ratios, text position (left/center/ configurable), mobile image.
  • Inline images in Static Content are not a fit for the S3 tool as-is (one image per record+suffix, writes a field, base editor cannot insert an image programmatically). Revisit with full Quill only if needed.

docs.title: Static Content
docs.text:
Purpose: Allow admins to place arbitrary rich-text content in any zone on any page, without building a dedicated LWC component. Use for banners, announcements, intro copy, or any static HTML content block.

Widget Type value: ust_static_content LWC: c-ust-static-content (built ✅) Zone-Ready: ✅ Active

How to use: 1. Open (or create) a UST_Portal_Widget__c record. The record page uses the UST Portal Widget Editor (ustWidgetRecordEditor), which replaces the classic layout. 2. Set Component Name = Static Content. The Content section appears. 3. Enter an optional header, pick a Content CSS Class (optional), and write the content in the rich text editor. Use the Paragraph style dropdown for Heading 2-5. The preview below the editor shows how it renders on the portal. 4. Set Zone, Page Context, Sort Order, and Is Active as normal, then Save.

Content CSS Class (Content_CSS_Class__c): styles the whole widget (not selected text). The classic Quill-based editor cannot round-trip a class attribute, so styles are widget-wide. Current values: ust-content-callout, ust-content-inverse, ust-content-centered, ust-content-muted. Only inherited properties (text color, alignment, font size) reach the rich text itself, because lightning-formatted-rich-text owns its markup.

Adding a new style class: (1) add a picklist value on Content_CSS_Class__c (API name = CSS class), (2) add it to ALLOWED_CONTENT_CLASSES in ustStaticContent.js, (3) add its rule in ustStaticContent.css. Classes not on the allowlist are ignored.

Adding a conditional section to the editor later: add the Component_Name__c value and a section key to COMPONENT_SECTIONS in ustWidgetRecordEditor.js, then add a getter and template block (see the header comment in that file).

Zone and page targeting: The editor's Page Context picker only offers pages that have the selected zone. It reads the UST_Portal_Zone_Placement__c registry, which ustWidgetZone keeps current by registering itself whenever an admin opens a page in Experience Builder (never for site visitors). Changing the zone removes known pages that lack it, with an Undo. Pages not yet registered can be typed in by page API name (lowercase, for example my_account__c). Admins need the UST_Portal_Widget_Admin permission set for registration to work. The banner and above_footer zones live in the shared theme layout (set Zone Scope = Layout on any zone placed there) and count as present on every page. See docs/WIDGET-AUTHORING-PLAN.md.

Components: - ustPageContextPicker - the page/zone-aware Page Context chooser used by the editor. - ustRichTextEditor is listed below. - ustWidgetRecordEditor - the record-page layout (Widget Setup, Content, Audience Filters) built on lightning-record-edit-form. - ustRichTextEditor - wraps lightning-input-rich-text and adds the Paragraph / Heading 2-5 dropdown (Heading 1 and 6 are deliberately excluded; the page already supplies the h1 and the widget header renders as an h2). It also shows a character counter against the 32,768 field limit. - Access: assign the UST_Portal_Widget_Admin permission set to admins who manage widgets.

Data flow: - PortalWidgetController.getWidgetsForZone() includes Static_Content__c and Content_CSS_Class__c in its SOQL query and maps them to PortalWidgetDto.staticContent / contentCssClass - ustWidgetZone.buildWidgetRegistry() passes both through to each widget object - ustWidgetZone.html renders <c-ust-static-content rich-text-content={widget.staticContent} content-class={widget.contentCssClass}> when widget.isStaticContent is true - ustStaticContent renders the HTML using <lightning-formatted-rich-text> (XSS-safe platform renderer)

Notes: - No deployment needed to add new static content - all content is managed in widget records - The Static Content field is an Html type (32,768 character limit) - Only renders if richTextContent is non-empty (guarded by hasContent getter) - After a JS-only deploy, Lightning may serve a stale bundle: clear IndexedDB / Cache Storage and reload twice (about 20 seconds apart) - Known limitation: the Heading dropdown and class picker are not available through the standard (non-custom) page layout; use the record page

docs.title: 1. Profile Card
docs.text:
Purpose: Surface the alumni's own information on the portal. Give them confidence the portal "knows" them and let them keep their record current.

Features: - Display name, photo, college/school, graduation year, major/minor - Allow alumni to upload or update their own headshot (migrate current functionality) - Allow alumni to update their contact information (migrate current functionality) - Allow alumni to update their Business Info — ❓ field list TBD (employer, title, LinkedIn URL? confirm with data team — see ROADMAP Q1) - GO (Gift Officer) / UA (University Advancement) staff can also update the widget content - Show contact information (email, phone, city/state)

Personalization trigger: Always shown; content varies by Contact record

Data sources: - Contact (Name, Photo, Email, Phone, Mailing City/State) - hed__Affiliation__c → hed__Account__r (College/School) - EDA Program Enrollment (Major/Minor) - Business Info fields — ❓ TBD (Contact fields, related Account, or custom object)

Notes: - Photo upload requires Files + ContentDocument support in Experience Cloud - Business Info update scope needs clarification before building — could be Contact fields (Title, Company) or a richer business profile object - Consider privacy controls: alumni can choose what is visible to other alumni in the directory

docs.title: 2. Events — Upcoming & Registered
docs.text:
Purpose: Show events the alumni cares about — both registered events and events matching their preferences. Upcoming events are prioritized over history.

Features:

Upcoming Alumni-Hosted Events list: - Suggested events based on: geographic proximity, virtual preference, interest categories - "Willing to travel" filter to expand geo radius

Upcoming Non-Alumni Events list: - Events NOT hosted by UST Alumni (partner / community events) ❓ data source TBD — see ROADMAP Q2 - Filtering by geographic location and alumni location

Event Registrations — Upcoming: - List of events the alumni has already registered for (upcoming first, then past)

Alumni-Created / Managed Events (Phase 2): - Ability for an alumnus to create their own event and invite others - Requires process flow definition for approval ❓ see ROADMAP Q3 - Implemented as a Screen Flow embedded in the widget

Personalization triggers: - Event preference settings (virtual vs. in-person, category interests) - Alumni Mailing Address (for geo-based suggestions) - Past event attendance history

Data sources: - CampaignMember (event registrations) - Campaign (event details, type, location, date) - Alumni preference record (virtual preference, interest categories) - Contact Mailing Address

Notes: - "Alumni-created events" feature is a future enhancement — requires a community-facing event creation flow - Campus ESP integration possible for parent-specific events (see St. Thomas Connection widget)

docs.title: 3. Give / Donor Widget
docs.text:
Purpose: Inspire giving through personalized storytelling. Surface the alumni's giving history and provide a prominent, contextual way to give.

Features: - Give button with seasonal impact storytelling (college/school-specific) - Highlight Tommie Give Day with enhanced messaging during that period - Show how past gifts have had real-world impact (impact stories) - Calendar year-end giving summary - Show gift receipts ❓ need definition of what information to show and where it is in SF - Show pledges ❓ need definition of what information to show and where it is in SF - Link to Endowment Reports and Impact Reports ❓ need definition - "Giving Society" membership badge (if applicable) - Donor: surface a personalized thank you message (see ROADMAP Q12 — Jira ECRMSF-5238)

Assigned Gift Officer section (Phase 1): - Show the alumni's assigned Gift Officer with photo and contact information - Allow GO/UA staff to update their own widget content - ❓ What fields? (Name, photo, phone, email, calendar booking link?) — see ROADMAP Q8 - ❓ Where does GO data live today — on the User record, a Contact relationship, or a custom object?

Personalization triggers: - Donor status (any gift on record) - College/School affiliation (for impact story targeting) - Giving society membership - Time of year (seasonal storytelling, Tommie Give Day calendar event)

Data sources: - Opportunity / NPSP giving records - ContentDocument (impact reports, endowment reports, gift receipts as files) - Custom Impact Story object or CMS content (seasonal stories by college) - Giving Society custom object or field on Contact

Notes: - Impact story content will likely be managed as Experience Cloud CMS content or a custom object - Tommie Give Day date should be stored in org configuration (Custom Metadata or Custom Setting) so the widget activates automatically

docs.title: 4. Engagement Summary (Year in Review)
docs.text:
Purpose: Show alumni their engagement across all four CASE pillars — giving, volunteering, events, and communications — as a motivating year-in-review summary.

Features: - Annual summary of engagement across CASE pillars: - Philanthropic: total giving amount, gift count - Volunteer: hours volunteered, roles filled - Experiential: events attended, workshops completed - Communications: emails opened, portal visits, social interactions - Engagement score visualization (existing framework) - "Next step" suggestions to increase engagement level - Incentive/gamification element: show progress toward next tier

Personalization triggers: All CASE activity tied to the Contact record

Data sources: - NPSP Opportunity rollups (giving totals) - Volunteer hours object (custom or NPSP Volunteers) - CampaignMember with attendance flag (events) - Email engagement (Salesforce Marketing Cloud or individual email results) - Existing engagement score model fields on Contact

Notes: - The engagement score model should already exist in the org — query Contact for the scoring fields rather than rebuilding - Year-end cutoff: calendar year (Jan 1–Dec 31) or fiscal year (confirm with advancement team)

docs.title: 5. St. Thomas Connection Messages
docs.text:
Purpose: Surface role-specific messages that acknowledge the alumni's special relationship with UST beyond just being a graduate.

Segment → Message mapping:

Segment Message Type Donor Personalized thank you message (see Give widget) Faculty / Staff Special recognition message for those who went on to serve UST Parent Link to CampusESP portal for parent-specific content General Default St. Thomas pride / community message

Personalization triggers: - Donor flag / giving history - Faculty/Staff flag (custom field on Contact or Relationship record) - Parent flag (custom field or relationship to current student)

Data sources: - Contact type fields (custom flags or EDA Affiliation types) - CampusESP URL (static link, stored in Custom Setting)

Notes: - These messages may be managed as CMS content so the advancement team can update copy without a code deploy - A Contact can fall into multiple segments — priority order: Donor > Faculty/Staff > Parent > General

docs.title: 6. Preference Center
docs.text:
Purpose: Let alumni control what they see on the portal and how UST communicates with them. Preferences also feed the newsletter content and event recommendations.

Features: - Content preferences: event types (virtual, in-person, career, athletics, philanthropy, etc.) - Channel preferences: Email, SMS, Phone, Mail, Social - Geographic preference: home city/region, willingness to travel - Newsletter opt-in/opt-out - Changes saved back to the Contact/preference record in real time

❓ Content type list: The 2026 CSV notes that content types need to align with existing SFMC "Filters and Sender Keys." This list must be pulled from the SFMC account before building the preference UI — see ROADMAP Q7.

Personalization triggers: N/A — this widget drives the personalization of others

Data sources: - Custom Alumni_Preference__c object (or fields on Contact) - Existing preference fields in org (confirm with team)

Notes: - Patrick noted this would be out of scope initially for a full real-time preference center; a simplified version (event type + channel opt-out) is the phase 1 target - Preferences should feed Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) subscriber attributes where applicable - This widget is key to the newsletter strategy: preferences → newsletter content → newsletter drives alumni back to portal

docs.title: 7. Alumni Directory & Connect
docs.text:
Purpose: Help alumni find and connect with each other. Enable one-to-one messaging and group connections.

Features: - Searchable directory of other alumni (opt-in visibility) - Filters by college/school, graduation year, major, city - Send a direct message to another alumnus (portal message or email) ❓ see note on PeopleGrove below - Alumni Notes / Story sharing with photos - Alumni-to-alumni event invitations

Personalization triggers: - Alumni's own visibility preferences (opt-in to directory) - Shared college, class year, major (for "people like you" suggestions)

Data sources: - Contact records with Community User accounts - Privacy preference flag (directory opt-in) - CommunityMessage__c or Experience Cloud Chatter for messaging — TBD on approach

Notes: - St. Thomas Connect (PeopleGrove) already exists as a platform for alumni-to-alumni connection - ❓ Phase 1 decision needed: native portal messaging vs. deep-link into PeopleGrove — see ROADMAP Q4 - Phase 1: Link to St. Thomas Connect with a deep-link into relevant groups/connections (default assumption until Q4 is resolved) - Phase 2: Native portal directory with filtered search - LinkedIn city-based groups also exist (Tommie Tailgates) — surface relevant group links by geo

docs.title: 8. Links Hub
docs.text:
Purpose: A curated set of quick-access links to the most common alumni needs and external systems.

Suggested Links (all Phase 1 unless noted):

Category Link Target System Notes Career Job listings / career coaching Handshake Career Alumni professional network St. Thomas Connect (PeopleGrove) Career Career services connection Handshake or St. Thomas Connect Academics Request a transcript Registrar system Academics Regent / financial aid processing Cloud for Good / Regent Athletics Athletics events UST Athletics site Athletics Purchase tickets Athletics ticketing system ❓ Paciolan? Personalization triggers: - Athletic ticket history → show ticket summary (Phase 2 / if data available) - College/school affiliation → surface relevant school directory link - Parent flag → show CampusESP link

Data sources: Mostly static links stored in Custom Metadata Type for admin management

docs.title: 9. Communications History
docs.text:
Purpose: Give alumni a single place to see all communications UST has sent them — no hunting through email inboxes.

Features: - List of emails sent via Salesforce or SFMC (with open/click status) - SMS sent — via Activity History ❓ or custom SMS object? confirm with CRM team - Individual Email Results (IER) from SFMC ❓ Marketing Cloud Connect must be configured — see ROADMAP Q9 - Filterable by date, type

Personalization triggers: All comms tied to the Contact record

Data sources: - EmailMessage (individual emails sent via SF) - SFMC Individual Email Results (synced to SF via Marketing Cloud Connect) - SMS_History__c (custom, if SMS is tracked)

Notes: - Farrah confirmed that anything sent via Salesforce or SFMC can be surfaced - SFMC data must be synced to the org via Marketing Cloud Connect for portal access

docs.title: 10. Photo & Story Sharing
docs.text:
Purpose: Let alumni share their life updates, stories, and photos — building a sense of community and giving advancement team rich content for storytelling.

Features: - Upload personal photos and life event photos ❓ does upload need an approval workflow? - Write "Alumni Notes" (short story/update) (migrate existing functionality) - Optionally share notes publicly with the alumni community - Profile photo upload (also used in Profile Card widget) - Event photo galleries — show photos from events the alumnus attended (photos must be tagged to that event/campaign) ❓ when should they show? who tags photos?

Personalization triggers: Alumni's own submissions

Data sources: - ContentDocument / ContentVersion (file uploads) - Custom Alumni_Story__c or Alumni_Note__c object - Contact.PhotoUrl (profile photo)

Notes: - Photo upload in Experience Cloud requires proper community sharing rules and file size limits - Moderation workflow may be needed if notes are publicly visible - The 5 Ts of Philanthropy framework (Time, Treasure, Talent, Ties, Testimony) — "Testimony" maps to this widget

docs.title: 11. Athletics
docs.text:
Purpose: Surface athletics content for alumni who care about UST sports.

Features: - Upcoming athletics events calendar - Link to purchase tickets (Athletics ticketing system) - Show tickets previously purchased (if data is available via integration) - Integration with UST Athletics ticketing platform

Personalization triggers: - Self-declared interest in athletics (preference center) - Past ticket purchase history (if available)

Data sources: - Integration with Athletics ticketing system (TBD — API or data sync) - Campaign records for athletics events (if tracked in Salesforce)

Notes: - Ticketing integration is flagged as a future/nice-to-have — phase 1 likely a link with ticket history if accessible

docs.title: 12. Videos & Media
docs.text:
Purpose: Embed curated video content and photo galleries on the portal — pride-building content that makes alumni feel connected to the UST community.

Features: - Top 10 playlist (curated videos — speaker series, highlights, campaigns) ❓ who manages this? UA/comms team via CMS? - Event photo galleries (especially photos from events the alumni attended) - Embedded video player (YouTube, Vimeo, or hosted)

Personalization triggers: - Events the alumni attended → show photos from those events - College/school affiliation → show relevant school videos

Data sources: - External video platform (YouTube/Vimeo embed links stored in CMS or Custom Metadata) - Event photo galleries (CMS content or ContentDocument linked to Campaign)

Notes: - Phase 1: Curated static playlist managed by the communications team - Future: Personalized gallery showing photos tagged to events the alumni attended

docs.title: 13. Volunteer Management
docs.text:
Purpose: Let alumni find, sign up for, and create volunteer opportunities — closing the loop on the CASE "Volunteer" pillar directly on the portal.

Phase: 2 — needs V4SF package decision first (see ROADMAP Q5)

Features: - Search and browse available volunteer opportunities - Sign up for opportunities directly from the portal - (Phase 2+) Alumni create their own volunteer opportunities — implemented as a Screen Flow embedded in the widget

Personalization triggers: - Alumni's interest categories (from Preference Center) - Past volunteer history

Data sources: - Volunteers4Salesforce (V4SF) managed package objects (if installed) — Volunteer_Job__c, Volunteer_Shift__c, Volunteer_Hours__c - ❓ If V4SF is not installed: custom object or NPSP Volunteers alternative

Notes: - ❓ Key blocker: Is Volunteers4Salesforce already in the org? If not, this requires a procurement/install decision before development begins - If V4SF is not available, a lightweight custom object could be built, but that duplicates what V4SF provides - "Create volunteer opp" flow needs approval process definition before scoping

docs.title: 14. Alumni News & UST Updates
docs.text:
Purpose: Keep alumni informed about what is new with UST and provide a space for ambassador-style storytelling — "proud to be part of the community" content.

Phase: 1 — but content source must be confirmed first (see ROADMAP Q11)

Features: - Alumni News section — curated content that UA can update without a code deploy - UST Updates — easy access to what is new at UST - "Alumni Ambassador" content — stories celebrating alumni achievement and UST community pride - Social media follow section — links to UST's active channels ❓ links needed from comms team

Personalization triggers: - College/school affiliation → show school-specific news - Interest preferences (from Preference Center)

Data sources: - ❓ TBD — could be Experience Cloud CMS, a custom News_Item__c object, or an RSS feed from the UST website - Social media links — static, stored in Custom Metadata for admin management

Notes: - This widget is distinct from the Videos & Media widget (Widget 12) — this is text/article content; Widget 12 is video/photo - UA team needs to be able to manage content without a developer; CMS is the preferred approach - Coordinate with comms team to confirm where "new with UST" content currently lives

Tommie tailgates – certain city even messages – such as events and maybe weather related. o Want to connect with alumni – one-to-one, also allow alumni to send message to group?  Could be a message on the portal? – user create their own widget o Link suggestions  Job Listings – Handshake or connection to career services – just a link – St. Thomas Connect.  Link to Athletics  Link to request a transcript  Link to website – other ways to engage – referral of students. How they want to engage with St. Thomas. Ways to surface up volunteer opportunities.  Bookstore online sales – customize options – maybe a link. Action related options (Ted’s suggestion) 5 Ts in philanthropy (Time, Treasure, Talent, Ties and Testimony)

  • Sharing their story. Provide means to enter this. With Alumni Notes. With uploaded photos.
  • Give button – with seasonal impact story telling based on college/school especially around Tommie Give Day. Can show how past given has impacted in real world...
  • Calendar year end giving summary
CASE metrics – based on 4 pillars (Philanthropic, Volunteer, Experiential (attendance to
events, workshops,etc), Communications (open rates, social media interactions, website visits,
etc).
  • Show list of events that the user already registered for. Upcoming is more important than history.
  • Show year end engagement summary – events attended / year wrap – all engagement. – Provide incentives of engagement to always have a step forward. Score model, use what is already developed – use existing frameworks.
  • News and information section – have alum be an ambassador – want to have proud to be part of the community. Give them easy access to what is new with UST. Follow us on our social channels.

configured to use campus SSO or use another system to authenticate? The native SF
login uses federated ID on user record to control what is used for SSO. Normally the
federated ID is a personal email address for community users.

Preferences in portal could be used for alumni newsletter content – use newsletter
to drive them back to the portal. Simplify communications – for preferences.
